Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We're happy to deliver a 48-hour sample and the export SOP. Quick notes:

- We'll provide: an anonymized CSV with event_type, timestamp_utc, request_id, obfuscated_user_id, resource, outcome, and extra (truncated).
- Redaction: user identifiers are hashed with a per-customer salt (one-way), IP addresses and full email addresses are redacted unless the customer has requested raw logs under contract.
- Delivery: standard options are S3 presigned URL (7-day expiry, optionally rotated daily) or customer-provided SFTP endpoint (mutual TLS). We can also push to a customer-owned S3 bucket via a temporary IAM role if requested.
- Retention: raw event retention in-host is 90 days; aggregated/metrics retention is 365 days (we can export raw up to 90 days).

I'm looping in Rishi for the compliance mapping and David for the export SOP and the sample file. Expect the CSV + instruction PDF by EOD Wednesday. If you need specific event types beyond the common set, let us know.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex/Jasmine — adding compliance context for SIG mapping: 

- SOC 2 control mapping: our audit events map to CC6 (system operations) and CC7 (change management); examples included in the extract show config.change and admin.role.update correlated to the user performing the change.
- Retention & access: customer access to logs is supported via time-bounded exports; we do not grant direct live tenant access to raw host logs. Exports are logged, and export artifacts are tracked in an export-audit index for 12 months.
- Redaction rules: PII fields (email, phone) are redacted by default; we can offer pseudonymization with HMAC-SHA256 using customer salt for customers with contractual need to re-identify. That workflow requires a signed data access addendum.
- Chain-of-custody: all presigned URL generations are recorded with who/what triggered the export; we include a manifest file alongside CSVs that lists event range, record count, and hash (sha256) for integrity verification.

@Laura — can you attach the export SOP and a small sample CSV (10 lines) with synthetic content? I'll annotate which SIG question IDs these map to for the evidence package.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Applied Security — Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — attaching the sample and the export SOP as requested. Highlights from the SOP: 

- Export methods: presigned S3 (recommended) | SFTP (fallback) | push-to-customer-bucket (requires IAM setup).
- Presigned rules: default expiry 7 days; we can set 24h for sensitive accounts. Generation requires an IAM service principal and is rate-limited.
- Manifest & integrity: each export includes a manifest.json (sha256 checksums) and a short readme describing which fields are redacted.
- Delivery logging: all export requests are logged to an immutable index; retention for export audit events is 12 months.
- Sampling: the sample CSV is synthetic but uses the same schema we export. Real extracts will follow pseudonymization rules unless a data addendum allows re-identification.

See attached: audit-log-sample-20260615.csv (10 synthetic rows) and sig-evidence-extract-instructions.pdf. Happy to run through these on a quick call if that helps.

Laura Bennett
Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
